item.title: A gentle introduction to Git worktrees
item.content:encoded: Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches into separate directories simultaneously, making parallel local development straightforward whether you're working solo or alongside AI coding agents.

item.title: Testing Android apps with Expo on physical devices
item.content:encoded: Learn how to connect your Android device via USB to your local Expo development server for reliable, production-like testing of your React Native apps.

item.title: GitHub Copilot's pricing gamble
item.content:encoded: GitHub's switch to usage-based Copilot pricing is a calculated bet that competitors will follow suit before too many users defect.

item.title: Creating a VS Code agent hook to respond to file changes
item.content:encoded: Learn how to use a VS Code agent hook to detect edits to a specific file and trigger deterministic follow-up automation.

item.title: Improving developer velocity with GitHub merge queue
item.content:encoded: GitHub merge queue reduces the manual churn of keeping pull requests current by automatically retesting them in order before merge.

item.title: Proxying fetch requests in server-side JavaScript
item.content:encoded: Learn how to proxy fetch() requests in Node.js, Deno, Bun, and Cloudflare Workers to better monitor and control your server-side traffic.

item.title: The importance of artifacts in AI-assisted programming
item.content:encoded: Your AI pair programmer has no memory, which is why proper documentation matters more than ever in AI-assisted development.

item.title: From Coder to Orchestrator: The future of software engineering with AI
item.content:encoded: The software engineering job of the future won't involve writing code; it will involve orchestrating AI agents to write code for you.
